source.title: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems

confidence_rationale: Canonical source for the two principles MECH-067 is re-deriving: COMPLETE MEDIATION (every access to every object must be checked for authority, with no bypass path) and FAIL-SAFE DEFAULTS (base access decisions on permission rather than exclusion, so the default is deny). The mapping is near-exact and the provenance value is real -- MECH-067 should be registered as an application of a fifty-year-old protection principle to an agent's internal write loci, not as a novel mechanism hypothesis. But confidence is capped at 0.5 on purpose: this is a normative design principle, not an empirical finding. It says what to build if you want an enforceable policy; it cannot establish that REE's existing local gates are currently insufficient, which is the empirical content of MECH-067 and the thing only the audit spike can settle.
failure_signatures: Any protection mechanism with a bypass path provides no guarantee: complete mediation requires that every access to every object be checked, and a design that checks 'most' accesses has the security properties of one that checks none.

A fail-open default (deny-listing what is forbidden rather than allow-listing what is permitted) fails in the unsafe direction, because an omission from the list silently grants rather than silently refuses -- and omissions are the expected steady state of a hand-maintained list.
Protection mechanisms that are psychologically unacceptable or that impose overhead on routine work get bypassed or disabled by their users, so a correct-but-costly gate is not durably a gate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Protection mechanisms should be designed according to eight principles, of which two are directly at issue: COMPLETE MEDIATION -- every access to every object must be checked for authority, and the design must supply no mechanism for bypassing the check; and FAIL-SAFE DEFAULTS -- access decisions should be based on permission rather than exclusion, so that a design or implementation mistake results in refused access rather than granted access.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-067's 'default-deny (phase, store, actor) matrix' is fail-safe defaults plus complete mediation, restated for an agent's internal stores. The typed store classes the claim proposes (POL / ID / CAPS / residue / attribution ledger / scratch) are the 'objects'; the phase is a dimension Saltzer and Schroeder did not need because an OS has no sleep cycle, but it is the same kind of coordinate. The claim's contention that per-site gates are not enough is the complete-mediation principle's negative half: a check that a caller may or may not route through is by definition not complete mediation, because the design supplies a bypass.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A normative principle is not evidence. This paper tells REE what a sound write-protection design looks like; it cannot tell REE whether the current local gates in ree_core are leaking, and MECH-067's 'required' is an empirical assertion about THIS substrate, not a restatement of good practice. There is a live risk of confirmation-by-authority here: citing Saltzer and Schroeder makes the matrix sound obligatory without any measurement having been taken, which is precisely the move MECH-067's own SUBSTRATE note guards against ('the audit is the spike that decides whether the build is owed'). Note also that the same paper supplies principles that cut the OTHER way -- ECONOMY OF MECHANISM and PSYCHOLOGICAL ACCEPTABILITY both argue against adding a policy object nobody has yet shown to be necessary.
mapping.source_context: Foundational computer-security tutorial and survey; Multics-era operating systems; no empirical study, no measurements.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality high as a canonical, still-taught reference, but the class is 'design principle' not 'result', which is why the aggregate (0.5) sits well BELOW the component mean rather than near it -- for a claim asserting empirical necessity, a normative source can only supply framing. transfer_risk 0.45: the principles were derived for adversarial multi-user OS protection, and their cost-justification does not automatically hold for an accidental-leak setting inside a single research substrate.
